We give counterexamples to a conjectured characterization of generically universally rigid graphs from [ 7 ] . We introduce a new operation that preserves the universal rigidity of generic frameworks and use it to construct infinite families of counterexamples. We also show that the so-called degree-2 extension operation preserves the property of being not universally rigid, for d = 1 d=1 . This operation is applied in the proof of a new lower bound on the size of generically universally rigid graphs.
